correctness.rationale: For all real t>0 the spherical monomial norm gives the displayed exact gamma series. Integer-step gamma ratios reduce each coefficient after t^{-2d} scaling to a finite product, analytic in h=1/t. Normal convergence on |u|<=R, |h|<=h0 with Rh0²<1 rigorously gives the 1/t expansion. The 0F1 differential equation reduces the correction at each simple Bessel zero to 2(d+1)u_k F_d′(u_k); the analytic implicit function theorem yields u_{k,t}=u_k(1-2(d+1)/t)+O(t^{-2}). Local uniqueness plus conjugation ensures real negative zeros. Numerical recurrence tests d=2,3, k=1,2 and t=100,200,400 reproduce the predicted O(t^{-2}) behavior, but are not used as proof.

value.rationale: The Euclidean distance weight concentrates at the ball incenter and produces a non-Gaussian exponential radial Fock limit, unlike the classical Gaussian Bergman scaling. Locating the resulting kernel-zero pattern and proving every fixed zero shares the exact d-dependent first relative motion gives a useful spectral-geometric invariant: arbitrarily many genuine Lu Qi-Keng failures for all sufficiently large real (not just integer) exponents. Normal convergence with first correction is needed to justify zero persistence and its rate; the fixed-index result does not pretend to classify all zeros globally.
